title: JMAP MLS key-material capability
description: Define and implement a mimid JMAP capability for what JMAP Chat lacks: KeyPackage upload/claim, Welcome/Commit/Proposal delivery, GroupInfo fetch, mapped onto protocol-06 keyMaterial/update/notify/groupInfo. Write it up as a spec doc (candidate draft).
design:
# Plan for mimid-1wgh.12: provider-side urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:mimi (draft at jmap-chat-spec 5630c10)

Status: APPROVED by Mark 2026-10-18 (decisions JM-1 .12.19, JM-2 .12.20, JM-5 .12.21, JM-4 and JM-6..11 below).

## Orchestrator corrections (applied below)
- JM-3 is superseded by Mark's 2026-10-18 decision: ChatContact.id is a server-assigned RFC 8620 Id, and login holds the URI (hub contact: login = the hub provider URI).
- Chat.id: base JMAP Chat L486 requires ULIDs assigned by the creating server. Mint a ULID once per (account, room) and store it, so a rebind finds the same Chat. The agent reuses it (J2). The plan's original "deterministic base64url hash" is dropped.

## 0. Summary
Most of the work is adapting code that already exists. The draft's methods map almost one-to-one onto it:
- `Follower::relay_*` gives Room/update, Room/send, GroupInfo/fetch and KeyMaterial/fetch.
- `Hub::create_room` gives Room/create, and already takes ratchetTree separately.
- `KeyPackages` gives KeyPackage/get,set; `Follower::leave` gives Room/unbind.
- The per-room follower log, with per-user membership and claim-gated Welcome visibility, gives Chats and Messages.

New work:
- the JMAP HTTP surface, bearer auth and an account model;
- a read projection of the follower log as JMAP Chats, Messages and ChatContacts, with state strings;
- EventSource push (a MUST in draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §Push);
- the Room/create checks (D2);
- the KeyPackage quota and last-resort replacement;
- .7.31.

Blocking conflict: the draft uses client URIs as credential identities, but H1 (.6.1) makes the identity the user URI (JM-1).

## 1. Scope: draft sections to beads
| Draft section | Bead | Action |
|---|---|---|
| whole draft | .12.1 | close (committed at 5630c10) |
| capability, keypackage objects, all args/responses, examples | .12.2 types crate (crate-jmap) | rewrite against 5630c10 (Room/send, Room/unbind, no epochTooOld SetError, string response codes, separate ratchetTree, message/mls); needs Mark's OK to write crate-jmap |
| keypackage, keypackage-claim | .12.3 | rewrite: overQuota; a new last-resort replaces the old one (the store refuses it today as SecondLastResort); reject a lastResort that disagrees with the bytes; KeyPackage state string and StateChange on create/destroy/claim |
| room-create, chat-roomid | .12.4 | rewrite: D2 checks in the JMAP handler (one leaf, one participant, room_uri = roomIdPrefix + base32 of 16 octets, 16-octet group ID); creator membership written atomically with the room |
| keymaterial-fetch | .12.5 | light rewrite: argument checks, response to JSON; drop the .12.3 dependency |
| room-update | .12.6 | re-scope to Room/update only; the fanout projection moves to .11.3 |
| room-send | .12.7 | rewrite as Room/send; sendingUri = userUri |
| groupinfo-fetch | .12.8 | keep; decode status; pass response through |
| room-unbind | NEW .12.19 | Room/unbind calls Follower::leave |
| e2e | NEW .12.20 | two providers driven only through JMAP, with mls-rs clients |
| fixedMembership | .12.18 | already closed (J3) |
| mls-messages, fanout-messages | .11.3 | Message projection, senderMsgId, hub ChatContact, Message/set refusals |

The provider needs a minimal base JMAP Chat subset (.11; see JM-4):
- Session at /.well-known/jmap, /jmap/api, EventSource.
- Chat/get, /changes, /query (no filters).
- Message/get, /changes, /query (filter chatId only; queryChanges answers cannotCalculateChanges).
- ChatContact/get, /changes, for hub contacts only.
- Chat/set and Message/set registered only to refuse.
- Nothing else: no Space, ReadPosition, typing, presence, blobs, push subscriptions or WSS.

Rewrite .11 to this scope; its current text is stale.

## 2. Dependencies
- .7.31 lands before .12.6 and .12.7. Widen it with the draft's second dedup rule (unique (room, senderMsgId), in the same migration) and JM-9. Then .7.31 owns every change to store/follower_log.rs and follower/notify.rs, and .11.3 only reads.
- Every method bead needs .11.1–.11.3 and .12.2 (.11.x itself doesn't need .12.2: Chat.roomId goes through Chat.extra). .12.3 and .12.4 also need JM-1 and JM-2.
- Stale epic dependencies (.12.3/.12.4 on .4; .12.5 on .5/.6): replace them with the specific closed children, or drop them (not checked child by child).
- .32 (admin CLI) depends on .11.1's store API and is off the critical path; tests insert accounts directly.
- .7.1 still waits for .13; .12.20 is an earlier e2e that needs no agent.
- Migration numbers are fixed now; merge in this order:
  - 0004: .7.31 dedup columns
  - 0005: .11.1 accounts and tokens
  - 0006: .11.3 membership history
  - 0007: .12.3 KeyPackage state

## 3. Architecture
Modules in crates/mimid-server/src/jmap/:
- mod.rs: router, merged into http::router on the same listener (JM-11).
- auth.rs: the single JMAP authorization point. An axum extractor turns `Bearer` into Account { account_id, user: LocalUser }. It is the only non-test caller of LocalUser::authenticated.
- session.rs: the Session object; uploadUrl and downloadUrl answer 404 (Limitation: no blobs).
- api.rs: jmap_server dispatch with named limits. maxSizeRequest must cover base64 growth of MAX_BODY_LEN (about 4/3 × 4 MiB plus overhead); maxCallsInRequest; maxObjectsInSet.
- bus.rs: ChangeBus, fed by Follower::subscribe and KeyPackage writes.
- push.rs: EventSource (RFC 8620 §7.3: types, closeafter, ping).
- projection.rs: a JmapBackend for Chat, Message and ChatContact (not the full ChatBackend).
- methods/{chat_set, message_set, key_package, key_material, room_create, room_update, room_send, room_unbind, group_info}.rs: one file per method. .11.2 creates them as stubs, so each later bead edits only its own file.
- store/jmap.rs: all new SQL.

Auth and accounts:
- One JMAP account per local user: jmap_account (ULID account_id, UNIQUE user_uri).
- jmap_token holds SHA-256(token), account_id, created_at and revoked_at. Tokens are 32 random bytes in base64url; only the hash is stored and compared in constant time; the admin CLI (.32) issues them.
- Failures: a wrong, missing or revoked token gives 401; someone else's accountId gives accountNotFound.
- Tests: wrong identity rejected, a token canary, and Debug redaction.

Account capability:
- userUri
- roomIdPrefix = mimi://<domain>/r/
- hubSender = base64url(hub key || credential), through a public Hub accessor
- cipherSuites = [1]
- maxKeyPackages: config, defaulting to a named constant (INVENTED value)

supportedBodyTypes: text/plain (the core MUST) and application/mimi-fanout.

Projection:
- Chat:
  - one per (account, room) that ever had a follower_member row;
  - id is a stored ULID (orchestrator correction); kind "group"; roomId; members [];
  - name per JM-8; unreadCount 0 (Limitation);
  - unbinding is invisible on the Chat object.
- Migration 0006 adds left_seq and joined_at to follower_member, so an unbound Chat keeps its Messages. The JMAP queries are new store/jmap.rs functions; Follower::events and its tests stay unchanged.
- Message:
  - one per visible follower_event: since_seq <= seq < left_seq (or left_seq NULL), with a Welcome claim gate;
  - id = seq;
  - bodyType application/mimi-fanout; body = base64url of the stored bytes;
  - senderMsgId = ULID(hub ts, SHA-256(bytes)[0..10]);
  - sentAt = hub ts; receivedAt = arrival time;
  - senderId = the hub ChatContact.
- State strings:
  - Message state is "<max seq>.<max member rowid of the user>". /changes since s.m returns created events with seq > s, plus every visible event of a membership row with rowid > m.
  - The second term is needed because a relayed join snapshots since_seq before sending. It needs a regression test.
  - Messages are never updated or destroyed. Chat and ChatContact state is the user's maximum membership rowid. KeyPackage state is a per-user counter (migration 0007), bumped in the same transaction as each write.

## 4. Proposed decision beads (under .12)
- JM-1 (BLOCKING) Credential identity. Draft §keypackage and Room/create rule 2 say the credential identity is a client URI bound to the account; H1 says it is the user URI. (a) Revisit H1, which needs a client-to-user map the hub lacks. (b) Keep H1, and read "client URI" as mimid's derived client URI (.7.8); the binding table is the existing `client` table; ask Mark to reword the draft. Recommend (b).
- JM-2 Encoding of keyPackageRef and invalidProposals: base64url of the TLS encoding including the varint prefix (what KeyPackageRef::as_bytes holds), vs the raw 32-byte hash. Recommend TLS; ask for a draft example.
- JM-3 Hub ChatContact id: SUPERSEDED by Mark's gap-3 decision (jmap-chat-spec-ka7b): ChatContact.id is a per-server RFC 8620 Id; the raw identity goes in a new immutable server-set `identity` property; hub contact identity = login = hub provider URI. Spec text pending; plan against it but cite no spec text until committed.
- JM-4 Core subset: EventSource only (no WSS, no PushSubscription). Chat/set: create, destroy and every update forbidden (the draft only requires its listed keys; refusing more is a Limitation). Message/set: create gives invalidArguments; body/bodyType/reactions updates give invalidArguments; other updates and destroy are forbidden. No ChatContact/set, so blocked is always false. text/plain is advertised but never accepted.
- JM-5 crate-jmap dependency: a git-rev pin to github.com/MarkAtwood/crate-jmap (needs a pushed commit for jmap-mimi-types) vs waiting for a crates.io release. Recommend git rev. Unknown: what is currently published.
- JM-6 Hub errors other than unreachable: transport errors and 5xx give serverUnavailable; 4xx gives invalidArguments with a description.
- JM-7 Dedup scope: per room (mimid) vs per Chat (draft). They differ only for duplicates stored while an account was unbound, which it couldn't decrypt anyway. Recommend per room, as a Limitation.
- JM-8 Chat.name: always "" (no Observer on followers; clients read the name from MLS anyway) vs room_name from the hub's GroupContext for hosted rooms. Recommend "", as a Limitation.
- JM-9 FanoutMessage timestamp >= 2^48: refuse at /notify (400), extending TimestampOutOfRange; in .7.31's scope.
- JM-10 maxKeyPackages on last-resort replacement: count after the replacement, so a replacement never gets overQuota.
- JM-11 Listener: same listener, under /jmap/* and /.well-known/jmap.

Already settled: D1 (separate ratchetTree), D2 (JMAP handler), D3 (draft now matches the hub), D4 (.7.30), lastResort precedence, and Room/create atomicity (one store transaction).

## 5. Test strategy
1. Draft JSON (.12.2): every §examples example hand-copied, with real payloads in place of "...". Fixed direction: decode, compare, re-encode, then serde_json::Value equality. Committed before the types, with PROVENANCE (jmap-chat-spec 5630c10).
2. MLS bytes from mls-rs only:
   - KeyPackage cases: valid, last-resort, wrong suite, expired, non-Basic, wrong identity, duplicate, already handed out, lastResort mismatch, quota, replacement;
   - Room/create groups failing each of rules 1–7;
   - handlers driven with draft-shaped JSON; keyPackage and response come back byte-identical.
3. Hostile input:
   - base64 that is padded, standard-alphabet, has non-zero trailing bits, or decodes past MAX_BODY_LEN;
   - deep or huge JSON; too many calls or objects;
   - a foreign accountId;
   - a KeyMaterialRequest whose roomId or requestingUser mismatches the arguments;
   - calls on an unbound Chat;
   - a duplicate /notify giving one Message; the echo plus the stored copy giving one Message.
4. e2e (.12.20): two in-process providers on loopback. Each user is an mls-rs client talking to its provider only through JMAP over HTTP plus EventSource.
   - Flows: KeyPackage/set → Room/create → cross-provider KeyMaterial/fetch → Room/update (Add + Welcome) → Welcome Message → join → Room/send both ways → remove → Room/unbind → GroupInfo/fetch plus external join.
   - Oracles: equal epoch_authenticator and exporter, equal plaintext, the removed client sees its removal, and StateChange arrives before /changes.
   - Caveat: under H1, the external-join leg needs a permissive mls-rs IdentityProvider. Uncertain.

## 6. Bead breakdown (decompose-just-in-time)
Now: file JM-1 to JM-11 (minus JM-3). JM-1, JM-2, JM-4 and JM-5 block the build.

Next, in detail:
- .11.1 JMAP accounts, tokens, auth (store/jmap.rs, migration 0005, jmap/auth.rs). Runs in parallel with .12.2 and .7.31.
- .11.2 JMAP HTTP surface (jmap/{mod,session,api,bus}.rs, method stubs, config, a one-line merge in http.rs and main.rs). Needs .11.1 and JM-5.
- .7.31, widened (senderMsgId uniqueness, JM-9). Runs in parallel.
- .11.3 Read projection (projection.rs, chat_set/message_set, migration 0006, store/jmap.rs queries; the join-below-state regression test). Needs .11.2, .7.31, JM-4, JM-7 and JM-8.
- .12.2 types crate (needs Mark's OK to write crate-jmap). Runs in parallel.

Later, one line each:
- .11.4 EventSource. Needs .11.3; runs in parallel with the methods.
- .12.3, .12.4 and .12.5 run in parallel on disjoint files: .12.3 needs JM-1, JM-2 and JM-10; .12.4 edits hub/mod.rs for atomic membership; .12.5 needs JM-6.
- .12.6 (Room/update), .12.7 (Room/send) and .12.8 (GroupInfo/fetch) need .12.4; .12.6 and .12.7 also need .7.31. .12.19 (Room/unbind) needs .11.3. All four run in parallel.
- .12.20 e2e via JMAP needs everything above plus .11.4.
- Then close .12 and remove the "No JMAP endpoint is served yet" Limitation.

Uncertain:
- what crate-jmap has published;
- whether the .4/.5/.6 children still cover anything needed;
- the mls-rs identity-provider workaround;
- that jmap_server handle_get/handle_query work with JmapBackend alone (not compiled yet).

1. Message.id must be a receiver-assigned ULID (base L588, L597), not seq. Mint a monotonic ULID per follower_event at insert (column in 0004 or 0006); keep seq as the internal cursor.
2. unreadCount: with no ReadPosition, base L545 counts all messages as unread, so 0 is wrong; lastMessageAt (L541) also changes per message, so Chat state must fold in the message cursor. Either serve correct values or record a base nonconformance.
3. JM-4 incomplete. Further base nonconformances to record or fix: Chat/set per-user updates (L1021: muted, muteUntil, pinnedMessageIds, ...); ChatContact/set blocked/displayName (L963-969; mimi-00 L424 relies on blocking the hub); ReadPosition (L906, L1333-1347); and the same contradiction for application/mimi-fanout (advertised per mimi L156, rejected per L415, vs base L245). Widen jmap-chat-spec-mmcb.
4. .12.29 wrongly includes pins: pinnedMessageIds is shared group state, admin-only (base L518, L548). Reword to read position and mute only; pins unsupported or MLS state.
5. crate-jmap jmap_server is not conformant as-is: all backend errors become serverFail, so no unsupportedFilter (handlers.rs:322; base L1180); properties aren't filtered; anchor is ignored. mimid needs its own Message/query wrapper and properties filter, or Limitations. The backend must implement query for ChatContact too.
6. ChangeBus misses membership changes: add_follower_member and leave don't broadcast, so back-fill, new Chats, the creator's Chat and Room/unbind produce no StateChange. Membership writes must publish to the bus.
7. Membership write ownership: 0006's left_seq/joined_at writers live in follower_log.rs (leave, add_follower_member, Welcome insert), contradicting '.7.31 owns follower_log.rs, .11.3 only reads'. Hub::create_room writes no follower_member, so the creator has no Chat until .12.4. Name an owner; order .12.4 after it.
8. JM-9 also needed on the relay-accept path (sent to the .7.31 agent as within its approved scope).
9. JM-6 incomplete: hub-local HubError (no HTTP status), 429 (should be serverUnavailable, not invalidArguments), and RelayError::InvalidResponse (serverFail). Reuse the HubError->HTTP table at http.rs:239-283.
10. The body limit: DefaultBodyLimit(4 MiB) applies only to the protocol sub-router (http.rs:93); the JMAP sub-router needs its own limit, with a test at the limit.
11. hubSender accessor: a public accessor must return room::hub_sender's TLS ExternalSender encoding (room.rs:60, pub(super)), not signature_public_key's raw 32 bytes (mod.rs:218).
12. State-string constraints: .12.3 must never prune key_package_claim (Welcome visibility joins it), or must record Welcome recipients at store time; 0006 should add an explicit id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY to follower_member (implicit rowid may change on VACUUM).
